findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres skip disables the only integration coverage for this path in CI, so the instrumentation-server startup regression the test guards is never exercised in Drone. A regression in server startup against postgres lands silently; the TODO says 'works locally' so the failure is environment-dependent and will not be caught by any other test in the diff.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu hold for the duration of BuildIndex allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource to both execute bleve.New on the same directory before either writes b.cache. Two callers race on the same dir path under b.opts.Root: bleve.New on an already-created/index-locked directory fails or produces a torn index, and one caller's error surfaces as a failed index build that previously could not happen; the file-backed path (size > FileThreshold) is the affected branch.

[ADVISORY] Calling s.Init(ctx) inside NewResourceServer turns index construction and watcher startup into a blocking prerequisite of constructor success, using whatever ctx the constructor has in scope rather than a request-scoped one. Any transient backend failure during init (search.build listing resources, DB access) now fails process startup hard instead of the previous lazy per-call Init that could retry on the next request; operators get a crash-loop instead of a degraded-but-starting server.

[BUG] The new log line calls s.search.TotalDocs(), assuming the ResourceIndex value stored in searchSupport.search exposes TotalDocs; if that interface does not declare TotalDocs this file does not compile. Build fails with 's.search.TotalDocs undefined' unless the interface already carries the method; if it compiles via a narrower interface it is fine, but as written the call is only valid if TotalDocs is part of the field's declared interface.

[BUG] Reordering Init so search.init() runs before initWatcher() opens a window where mutations committed between the search index snapshot and watcher start are never indexed. Any write that lands after search.init() reads its snapshot but before initWatcher() begins streaming events is permanently missing from the index until a full rebuild — previously the watcher started first so those events were buffered; after this diff they are silently dropped, producing stale search results (missing dashboards/folders) in production with no error.

[BUG] Moving Init into NewResourceServer makes the synchronous full search-index build a hard startup path, so a slow or failing index build now blocks or aborts server construction instead of being surfaced per-request. Large namespaces that took minutes to index previously let the server start and serve Reads/Writes while init progressed via lazy Init; after this diff the constructor blocks for the entire build duration (startup/health-check timeouts, liveness kills) and any transient backend error during construction prevents the server from ever starting, with no retry path (s.initErr is one-shot).

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock that spanned the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to race, and the second bleve.New on the same on-disk directory fails. When the same NamespacedResource is rebuilt concurrently (e.g. two events for the same resource arriving before the cache entry exists), the file-based path calls bleve.New on an already-created directory and returns an error ('index already exists'), and the in-memory path wastes a full duplicate build — the pre-diff mutex serialized this.

[BUG] The only integration test exercising a storage-server target is now skipped for postgres, silently dropping that acceptance path from CI with only a TODO comment and no tracking issue in the diff. Regressions in the unified storage server against postgres (the primary production database) land undetected; this diff's own change — eager Init in NewResourceServer — is exactly the kind of startup-order change that would have surfaced there.

[ADVISORY] History and Origin still dereference s.search without the nil guard that Search has, and the diff removes their per-request Init calls without adding a nil check. On a server constructed without search support, History/Origin panic with a nil-pointer dereference instead of returning the 'search index not configured' error Search returns; before this diff the per-request Init at least consistently reached the same unguarded path, but the asymmetry with the adjacent Search guard (line ~915) is now the only thing preventing the crash and it is missing here.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds no test covering the new eager-Init-in-constructor behavior or the reordering of search.init before initWatcher. The two riskiest behavioral changes in this PR (startup ordering and lazy-to-eager init migration) ship unverified; a regression in either — such as the event-loss window or a constructor that now fails startup — would not be caught by any test in the diff.

[ADVISORY] init propagates the traced ctx (ctx, span := s.tracer.Start) into the background index-build goroutine, coupling the build's lifetime/cancellation to whatever context init was called with — now the constructor's ctx. If NewResourceServer's ctx is cancelled or times out mid-build (e.g. a caller using a request-scoped or timeout-bounded context), the index build is aborted and init returns an error that permanently sets s.initErr, bricking the server; the pre-diff discarded-ctx version was immune to caller cancellation.

[ADVISORY] Latency is computed from evt.ResourceVersion interpreted as UnixMicro against time.Now().UnixMicro(); if any producer stamps ResourceVersion as a millisecond or second RV the >5s warning fires spuriously for every event. Log noise and misleading 'high index latency' warnings at 1000x scale; low impact but the assertion has no guard on the unit convention and nothing in the diff verifies producers use UnixMicro.

[BUG] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously at construction, converting a lazy per-request init into a hard startup dependency that blocks construction until the full search index build and watcher start complete. Large deployments with big indexes (or a slow/unavailable DB at boot) block process startup for the entire index build duration; any transient DB error at boot now makes NewResourceServer return an error and aborts startup entirely, where previously the server would start and retry init per request.

[BUG] Init is invoked with whatever ctx NewResourceServer was handed, so the index build now inherits a possibly short-lived caller context instead of the request-scoped contexts it previously ran under. If the constructor is called with a context that is later cancelled (or a request-derived ctx), the index build and watcher setup are cancelled mid-flight, leaving initErr set and a permanently unsearchable server.

[ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu lock around the whole BuildIndex body removes the implicit serialization of index builds, so two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same file-backed key can both call bleve.New on the same directory. The second caller's bleve.New(dir) fails (or both race writing to the same index dir), turning a previously serialized path into a race that surfaces as spurious index-build errors under concurrent first-access; the author's rebuttal that cache set is the only shared state does not cover the shared on-disk directory.

[BUG] The postgres skip is unrelated scope drift for a storage-performance PR, and it permanently disables the integration test rather than fixing or time-boxing it. The instrumentation-server regression the test guards is no longer verified on postgres in CI; 'Works locally' with no tracking issue means the skip silently becomes permanent and a postgres-specific regression lands undetected.

[ADVISORY] Reordering search.init before initWatcher means watch events emitted between watcher start and index completion were previously handled by a running watcher ordering; the new order means the index build now runs before the watcher starts, widening the gap where writes landing during a long build are only caught by the (late-started) watcher. If the index build takes minutes, mutations committed during the build are replayed only after initWatcher finally starts; any event dropped or lost before the watcher attaches leaves the freshly built index stale until the next rebuild — a consistency invariant this diff no longer enforces.

[ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log uses time.Now().Unix() second-granularity duration, so any build under one second logs duration_secs 0 and is indistinguishable from a no-op. Operators using this new log line to gauge index build performance in small namespaces get useless zero values; the codebase's existing time.Since pattern would have given sub-second resolution.

[ADVISORY] Init-call removal from eleven public methods (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob/GetBlob) is traceable only to the new constructor-time Init; any other construction path for server that does not route through NewResourceServer now serves traffic with an uninitialized store and search. Any test helper, embedding caller, or alternate constructor that previously relied on lazy Init now returns results from an uninitialized backend (nil store/search panics or empty reads) instead of triggering initialization; the invariant 'every RPC path guarantees init' was enforced at 11 sites and is now enforced at exactly one.

[BUG] Removing cacheMu from around the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds of the same key, and the second bleve.New(dir) on the same file-backed path fails because bleve.New errors when the directory already contains an index. Two concurrent first searches for the same tenant (or a build racing a handleEvent-triggered rebuild) now return an 'index already exists' error for the file-backed path where the previous global lock serialized them; the caller gets a failed search/build instead of an index, and the losing goroutine's built index is discarded after doing the full document-scan work.

[BUG] Moving Init into NewResourceServer makes a full search-index build (which iterates and indexes every stored resource) a hard, synchronous prerequisite of process startup, converting what was previously a lazy per-request recoverable step into an unbounded blocking startup phase. A tenant with a large corpus (size > FileThreshold, i.e. a disk-backed bleve index per namespace) now blocks process start for the entire index rebuild; a slow or transiently failing backing store turns into a startup crash-loop instead of a degraded-but-serving server, and memory grows with total document count during the boot-time build (unbounded materialization on the startup path).

[BUG] Reordering initWatcher() to run after search.init() opens a gap where writes committed during the (potentially minutes-long) index build are never applied to the freshly built index if the watcher starts from the current RV. Search results are silently stale: any resource written between search.init()'s snapshot and initWatcher()'s stream position is missing from the index until some later write to that resource triggers a rebuild; the bleve.go TODO ('check last RV so we can see if the numbers have changed') indicates the rebuild-from-last-RV reconciliation this ordering depends on does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test for the storage-server-target instrumentation path is unconditionally skipped in CI with a 'works locally' note, so the exact scenario this diff changes (server construction now running Init, including search.init and initWatcher, before serving) has no CI coverage on a real SQL backend. A startup-ordering or postgres-specific initialization regression (e.g. Init failing on postgres, which is precisely the plausible cause of the 'works locally' failure) ships green: the build passes while the production postgres deployment of the storage server is broken.

[ADVISORY] All per-request Init calls are deleted, but Init remains an exported method whose initErr-latching contract ('retryable lazily, failure logged not returned') is now inconsistent with the constructor path where the same failure is fatal — two call paths with different failure semantics for the same initializer. Any caller (out-of-tree embedders, future internal code) that constructs the server without NewResourceServer's Init call, or that calls Init(ctx) with a caller-supplied context, gets a server whose handlers proceed against an uninitialized watcher/search with no error and no retry, silently returning empty/failed results instead of the previous init-error response.

[BUG] Moving Init from lazy per-request calls into NewResourceServer silently changes the failure model: init failures (search index build, watcher start) that previously left the server runnable and retryable per-request now abort construction entirely, and any server instance not built through this constructor loses initialization guarantees outright. A transient search-backend or DB hiccup during deploy becomes a hard startup crash instead of a degraded-but-serving instance; conversely, servers created by other construction paths (tests, alternate wiring) silently skip Init because the per-request calls were deleted without an invariant that NewResourceServer is the only entry point.

[BUG] Narrowing cacheMu to only the final cache insert removes the serialization of concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key, so two goroutines can both call bleve.New on the same directory path concurrently. The second bleve.New(dir) fails (bleve refuses to open/create an index that already exists at the path), turning a previously-serialized safe path into intermittent 'index already exists'-style errors under concurrent first access to the same namespace/resource; the cache also last-writer-wins, potentially discarding the fresher index.

[ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log line reports end-start where end is captured immediately after launching the background index-building goroutine, so duration_secs measures goroutine spawn time, not index build time. Operators triaging slow startups from the new log get a near-zero duration that contradicts IndexCreationTime and the actual work, eroding trust in the observability added by this PR.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is now unconditionally skipped in CI on the strength of an inline 'works locally' comment, so the exact code path this PR rewrites (eager Init at construction, reordered watcher/search init) has no CI coverage for the primary production database. A regression in Init ordering or blob/search wiring that only manifests on postgres lands undetected; the TODO has no linked issue, so the skip can persist indefinitely while this PR is the riskiest change to that path in the file's history.

[ADVISORY] Init moved from per-request lazy invocation into NewResourceServer turns a previously per-request recoverable init error into a hard constructor failure, changing the failure boundary for all ten ResourceServer methods that called Init. Any transient indexing/watcher failure at process start now prevents the server from being constructed at all; previously a failed Init was retried on the next request, so a slow or flaky index backend during a rolling deploy takes the storage server down instead of degrading per-request.

[ADVISORY] The only test change in this diff is a t.Skip() that disables the integration test for postgres with a TODO, removing CI coverage for a DB backend while the diff restructures server lifecycle (Init moved from lazy per-request calls into NewResourceServer, watcher/search init reordered). Any regression from the init reordering (e.g. Init failing at construction time, or the watcher now initialized after search) will no longer be caught by this integration test for postgres in CI; the skip masks an environment-specific failure ('Works locally') instead of fixing it, so the suite silently loses coverage while passing green.

[ADVISORY] Init is now called unconditionally in NewResourceServer, converting a previously lazy, per-request-retried initialization failure into a hard startup failure. If search.init or initWatcher fails at process start (transient DB/search-store unavailability, partially built index dir), the resource server cannot be constructed at all, so the pod crash-loops instead of serving degraded traffic and retrying; during a rolling deploy this turns a recoverable condition into an outage window.

[BUG] Removing the function-wide cacheMu lock in BuildIndex makes the b.cache[key] read and the build itself run concurrently for the same key, so two concurrent callers both construct an index for the same file-backed path and the second bleve.New(dir) fails with 'index already exists', and the unsynchronized map read/write on b.cache is a data race that can panic with 'concurrent map read and map write'. Two concurrent searches (or a search racing a WriteEvent-driven rebuild) for the same namespace/resource either crash the process on the map race or return a spurious build error to callers who previously serialized behind the lock; the cache dedup that justified the lock is now gone, so every concurrent caller pays the full reindex cost.

[BUG] Moving Init (which includes the full search index build and watcher startup) from the per-request lazy path into NewResourceServer turns a transient backend failure at construction time into a hard startup failure with no retry, whereas the removed per-request Init calls would have retried on the next request. A momentary database unavailability during process start now prevents the resource server from being constructed at all (process fails to start), instead of the previous behavior where the first request would re-attempt lazy initialization; conversely, any caller that constructs the server before the backing store is reachable can never recover because the retry points (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/IsHealthy) were all deleted.

[BUG] Init sets s.initErr and only logs it; when called from NewResourceServer the returned error path depends entirely on initErr propagating, but if any earlier step set initErr the search init and initWatcher are silently skipped with no per-step log, and IsHealthy (init check removed at line ~940) now reports diagnostics.IsHealthy without any indication that the search index or watcher never initialized. A server whose watcher failed to start (initErr set) serves reads/writes from the SQL backend while the search index permanently diverges from the data, and health checks report healthy, so operators get search results that silently miss recent writes with no signal that init ever failed.

[ADVISORY] Reordering initWatcher to run after s.search.init lengthens the window during which writes are not being watched while the (potentially long) full index build reads its snapshot, so events committed between the build's data read and the watcher's start position can be silently dropped from the index. The larger the tenant (longer init), the more writes fall into the unwatched gap; combined with the acknowledged 'TODO, check last RV' gap in bleve.go, those resources are missing from search results until a full rebuild, with no error or metric indicating the miss.

[ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log computes duration via time.Now().Unix() subtraction, so any init under one second logs duration_secs=0 and the IndexCreationTime histogram records 0, making the new observability signal useless for all but the slowest builds. Operators tuning index-build performance get a metric quantized to whole seconds (typically 0), and cannot distinguish a fast init from a failed/no-op one using this log line.

[ADVISORY] Changing to ctx, span := b.tracer.Start in GetResourceStats rewires the rest of the function's queries into the span's context, so the SQL stats query now runs under a child span context that will carry the span's cancellation into the request — harmless if the caller's ctx is the request ctx, but it means an early span.End() ordering mistake or span-based timeout would now cancel the DB query, a semantic change with no test coverage in this diff. If any future refactor moves span.End() earlier or attaches a span-scoped deadline, the stats query starts failing with context cancellation in ways the previous shadowed-ctx version did not; no regression test in this diff guards GetResourceStats behavior.

The diff also removes the per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls from History/Origin, so on a server where `s.search` is not configured (possible per `if s.initErr == nil && s.search != nil { s.initErr = s.search.init(ctx) }`), these methods would dereference a nil pointer and panic instead of returning the same error as Search.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes two concrete behavioral changes: (1) NewResourceServer now eagerly calls s.Init(ctx) and returns an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, added err := s.Init(ctx) block), while all per-RPC lazy Init calls were removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.; and (2) Init now initializes the search index before starting the watcher (order swapped around s.search.init(ctx) and s.initWatcher()). The only test change in the diff is adding a postgres skip in module_server_test.go; there are no new/updated tests exercising constructor-time init failure or the new init ordering. That makes the finding specific and diff-grounded as an unverified, nontrivial behavior change rather than a directly provable defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `_, span := s.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)` to `ctx, span := ...` in `searchSupport.init`/`build`, which only propagates the span context; the returned `ctx` is still derived from the original and shares the same cancellation semantics as before. Discarding the returned ctx previously did not make the work “immune” to caller cancellation—it merely failed to propagate the tracing context. Also, the claim about NewResourceServer’s ctx being request-scoped/timeout-bounded is not verifiable from this diff (we can see `s.Init(ctx)` was added, but not what `ctx` is).

The finding asserts producers may stamp `ResourceVersion` in ms/sec causing spurious warnings, but the diff provides no evidence about the unit convention or any producer behavior, so the claimed defect/log-noise risk cannot be verified from this PR diff alone.

Large deployments with big indexes (or a slow/unavailable DB at boot) block process startup for the entire index build duration; any transient DB error at boot now makes NewResourceServer return an error and aborts startup entirely, where previously the server would start and retry init per request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change initialization from lazy to eager: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and many RPC handlers no longer call `s.Init(ctx)`. This makes construction block on `Init`, which includes `s.search.init(ctx)` (index build) and `s.initWatcher()` (watch startup), so startup time/boot dependency concerns are valid. However, the finding’s claim that previously it would “retry init per request” is not supported: `Init` uses a one-time init pattern (`s.initOnce.Do(...)` with `s.initErr`), so after the first failure it would not retry on later requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Init is invoked with whatever ctx NewResourceServer was handed, so the index build now inherits a possibly short-lived caller context instead of the request-scoped contexts it previously ran under. If the constructor is called with a context that is later cancelled (or a request-derived ctx), the index build and watcher setup are cancelled mid-flight, leaving initErr set and a permanently unsearchable server.

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves one-time initialization from request handlers (multiple `if err := s.Init(ctx)` calls removed) into `NewResourceServer` via `err := s.Init(ctx)` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go). Since `Init` is guarded by `s.initOnce.Do`, any failure during that constructor-time init becomes sticky (`s.initErr` logged and reused), which could leave the server unusable. However, the finding’s key premise—that the `ctx` used in `NewResourceServer` is “possibly short-lived caller context”—is not verifiable from the diff because `NewResourceServer` does not take a context parameter and the origin/lifetime of the local `ctx` variable is not shown in the provided hunk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu lock around the whole BuildIndex body removes the implicit serialization of index builds, so two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same file-backed key can both call bleve.New on the same directory. The second caller's bleve.New(dir) fails (or both race writing to the same index dir), turning a previously serialized path into a race that surfaces as spurious index-build errors under concurrent first-access; the author's rebuttal that cache set is the only shared state does not cover the shared on-disk directory.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, the diff removes the `b.cacheMu` lock that previously wrapped the entire `BuildIndex` body and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. With this change, two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls can both proceed past the cache check/build path and, for file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), both compute the same `dir := filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ...))` and call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` concurrently. That introduces a real race on the shared on-disk index directory (not just the in-memory cache), which can lead to spurious build failures or corruption compared to the previously serialized behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The postgres skip is unrelated scope drift for a storage-performance PR, and it permanently disables the integration test rather than fixing or time-boxing it. The instrumentation-server regression the test guards is no longer verified on postgres in CI; 'Works locally' with no tracking issue means the skip silently becomes permanent and a postgres-specific regression lands undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an unconditional skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a comment “Works locally” and no issue/link or time-bounding (module_server_test.go). This reduces CI coverage for postgres and can allow postgres-specific regressions in the instrumentation-server behavior to go undetected. It’s a concrete review concern but not a runtime correctness defect in the shipped code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Reordering search.init before initWatcher means watch events emitted between watcher start and index completion were previously handled by a running watcher ordering; the new order means the index build now runs before the watcher starts, widening the gap where writes landing during a long build are only caught by the (late-started) watcher. If the index build takes minutes, mutations committed during the build are replayed only after initWatcher finally starts; any event dropped or lost before the watcher attaches leaves the freshly built index stale until the next rebuild — a consistency invariant this diff no longer enforces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go reorders initialization inside server.Init(): it now calls s.search.init(ctx) before s.initWatcher() (previously watcher started first). That is a real, diff-grounded change in consistency/ordering semantics for how the search index and watch-based updates are brought online. However, the finding’s stronger claim (that events during a long build will be lost/dropped and leave the index stale) is not directly verifiable from this diff because initWatcher’s start position/cursor semantics and search.init’s snapshot/version handling are not shown. It’s a concrete architectural/edge-case concern created by the change, but not provably a defect from the provided code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log uses time.Now().Unix() second-granularity duration, so any build under one second logs duration_secs 0 and is indistinguishable from a no-op. Operators using this new log line to gauge index build performance in small namespaces get useless zero values; the codebase's existing time.Since pattern would have given sub-second resolution.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, init() measures duration with start := time.Now().Unix() and end := time.Now().Unix(), then logs duration_secs as end-start. Unix() is second-granularity, so any init completing in <1s will log 0, reducing the usefulness of the new "search index initialized" log for small/fast indexes. This is a real, diff-grounded observability issue, but not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init-call removal from eleven public methods (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob/GetBlob) is traceable only to the new constructor-time Init; any other construction path for server that does not route through NewResourceServer now serves traffic with an uninitialized store and search. Any test helper, embedding caller, or alternate constructor that previously relied on lazy Init now returns results from an uninitialized backend (nil store/search panics or empty reads) instead of triggering initialization; the invariant 'every RPC path guarantees init' was enforced at 11 sites and is now enforced at exactly one.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes per-RPC lazy initialization (`if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }`) from many server methods (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob) and instead adds eager initialization in `NewResourceServer` (`err := s.Init(ctx)` with error return). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/architecture change: initialization is now guaranteed only when construction goes through `NewResourceServer`. The finding’s broader claim that there exist other construction paths that will now serve traffic uninitialized is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff alone (no alternate constructors/test helpers shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing cacheMu from around the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds of the same key, and the second bleve.New(dir) on the same file-backed path fails because bleve.New errors when the directory already contains an index. Two concurrent first searches for the same tenant (or a build racing a handleEvent-triggered rebuild) now return an 'index already exists' error for the file-backed path where the previous global lock serialized them; the caller gets a failed search/build instead of an index, and the losing goroutine's built index is discarded after doing the full document-scan work.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously took b.cacheMu for the entire function and now only locks when writing `b.cache[key] = idx` (lock removed at top; added just around the map write). This diff-grounded change can allow concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` to both proceed past cache checking/creation and attempt to create a file-backed index at the same `dir` (`bleve.New(dir, mapper)`), which is a classic race that can cause one build to fail or wastefully duplicate work before one overwrites the cache entry. The previous global lock serialized these builds; the new locking no longer does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Moving Init into NewResourceServer makes a full search-index build (which iterates and indexes every stored resource) a hard, synchronous prerequisite of process startup, converting what was previously a lazy per-request recoverable step into an unbounded blocking startup phase. A tenant with a large corpus (size > FileThreshold, i.e. a disk-backed bleve index per namespace) now blocks process start for the entire index rebuild; a slow or transiently failing backing store turns into a startup crash-loop instead of a degraded-but-serving server, and memory grows with total document count during the boot-time build (unbounded materialization on the startup path).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from a lazy per-request path to server construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure, while all the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed (e.g., in `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...`). `Init` synchronously calls `s.search.init(ctx)` when search is configured and logs errors, so this makes search/index initialization a hard prerequisite of creating the server and turns init failures into construction failures (potential crash-loop if the process cannot start). However, the finding’s claims about an “unbounded full search-index build”, “iterates and indexes every stored resource”, and “memory grows with total document count” are not directly verifiable from the shown diff alone (we don’t see what `search.init` does internally).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering initWatcher() to run after search.init() opens a gap where writes committed during the (potentially minutes-long) index build are never applied to the freshly built index if the watcher starts from the current RV. Search results are silently stale: any resource written between search.init()'s snapshot and initWatcher()'s stream position is missing from the index until some later write to that resource triggers a rebuild; the bleve.go TODO ('check last RV so we can see if the numbers have changed') indicates the rebuild-from-last-RV reconciliation this ordering depends on does not exist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly reorders initialization in `(*server).Init`: the watcher is now started **after** `s.search.init(ctx)` (see the moved block around `// Start watching for changes`), whereas previously the watcher started before the search index init. If `search.init` performs a long build and the watcher only begins streaming from “current” state when it starts, this ordering could plausibly miss updates that occur during the build window. However, the diff does not show `initWatcher()` or how the watch stream position/RV is chosen, nor how `search.init` snapshots data, so the claimed “never applied” staleness bug cannot be definitively verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test for the storage-server-target instrumentation path is unconditionally skipped in CI with a 'works locally' note, so the exact scenario this diff changes (server construction now running Init, including search.init and initWatcher, before serving) has no CI coverage on a real SQL backend. A startup-ordering or postgres-specific initialization regression (e.g. Init failing on postgres, which is precisely the plausible cause of the 'works locally' failure) ships green: the build passes while the production postgres deployment of the storage server is broken.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an unconditional skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a note that it fails in CI but works locally. In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` (which runs `s.search.init(ctx)` and `s.initWatcher()`) and removes the per-RPC `Init` calls. That is a meaningful startup/ordering behavior change for real SQL backends, and the only integration test covering the described instrumentation/storage-server-target path is now not exercised on postgres in CI. This creates a concrete, diff-grounded gap where a postgres-specific init regression could ship without CI catching it, but it’s not itself a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All per-request Init calls are deleted, but Init remains an exported method whose initErr-latching contract ('retryable lazily, failure logged not returned') is now inconsistent with the constructor path where the same failure is fatal — two call paths with different failure semantics for the same initializer. Any caller (out-of-tree embedders, future internal code) that constructs the server without NewResourceServer's Init call, or that calls Init(ctx) with a caller-supplied context, gets a server whose handlers proceed against an uninitialized watcher/search with no error and no retry, silently returning empty/failed results instead of the previous init-error response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes all per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls from handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` once in `NewResourceServer`, returning an error if init fails. `Init(ctx)` still exists as an exported method and internally latches `s.initErr` and logs on failure (seen in `Init`), which creates two distinct initialization usage patterns (constructor-fatal vs. callable method with its own context). While the diff doesn’t prove any current caller constructs `server` without `NewResourceServer`, the change does make initialization correctness depend on always using the constructor path, and the exported `Init` remaining callable with different semantics/context is a real, diff-grounded design concern rather than a demonstrable functional bug in the shown code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Moving Init from lazy per-request calls into NewResourceServer silently changes the failure model: init failures (search index build, watcher start) that previously left the server runnable and retryable per-request now abort construction entirely, and any server instance not built through this constructor loses initialization guarantees outright. A transient search-backend or DB hiccup during deploy becomes a hard startup crash instead of a degraded-but-serving instance; conversely, servers created by other construction paths (tests, alternate wiring) silently skip Init because the per-request calls were deleted without an invariant that NewResourceServer is the only entry point.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from per-request to construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure, while `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` removed their `s.Init(ctx)` calls. This definitely changes *when* failures surface (startup/constructor vs first RPC). However, the finding’s claim that the old model was “runnable and retryable per-request” is not fully supported by the diff: `Init` uses a one-time initialization pattern (`s.initOnce.Do(...)` with `s.initErr`), so prior per-request calls would not inherently “retry” after a transient failure. The concern about alternate construction paths bypassing `NewResourceServer` is plausible but not verifiable from this diff alone (we can’t see other constructors/usages).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Narrowing cacheMu to only the final cache insert removes the serialization of concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key, so two goroutines can both call bleve.New on the same directory path concurrently. The second bleve.New(dir) fails (bleve refuses to open/create an index that already exists at the path), turning a previously-serialized safe path into intermittent 'index already exists'-style errors under concurrent first access to the same namespace/resource; the cache also last-writer-wins, potentially discarding the fresher index.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire method (covering index creation via bleve.New/bleve.NewMemOnly and the builder work). The diff removes that broad lock and only locks around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` assignment. This change eliminates serialization of concurrent BuildIndex calls, so two goroutines can now concurrently execute the directory-backed `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` path for the same `key`/`dir` before either writes to the cache, which can lead to racey duplicate index creation/opening and nondeterministic last-writer-wins cache state. The diff itself shows the removed lock scope and the directory-backed creation path (`dir := ...; index, err = bleve.New(dir, mapper)`), making the concurrency hazard introduced by this change verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log line reports end-start where end is captured immediately after launching the background index-building goroutine, so duration_secs measures goroutine spawn time, not index build time. Operators triaging slow startups from the new log get a near-zero duration that contradicts IndexCreationTime and the actual work, eroding trust in the observability added by this PR.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, searchSupport.init() records start := time.Now().Unix(), then launches work in a background goroutine (the `go func() { ... }()` block), and immediately after sets end := time.Now().Unix() and logs `"search index initialized"` with duration_secs = end-start. From the diff, that duration is measured before the goroutine completes, so it reflects only time to kick off async work, not the actual index build. This is a misleading observability signal rather than a functional defect. (Note: IndexCreationTime in the same block also uses end-start, so the claim that the log contradicts that metric is not supported by the shown diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is now unconditionally skipped in CI on the strength of an inline 'works locally' comment, so the exact code path this PR rewrites (eager Init at construction, reordered watcher/search init) has no CI coverage for the primary production database. A regression in Init ordering or blob/search wiring that only manifests on postgres lands undetected; the TODO has no linked issue, so the skip can persist indefinitely while this PR is the riskiest change to that path in the file's history.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an unconditional skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a comment "test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally." This removes postgres coverage for that integration test in CI, and the TODO/skip has no linked issue or tracking reference in the diff, so it can linger indefinitely. While the claim about postgres being the primary production DB isn’t verifiable from the diff, the CI-coverage regression caused by the new skip is directly grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init moved from per-request lazy invocation into NewResourceServer turns a previously per-request recoverable init error into a hard constructor failure, changing the failure boundary for all ten ResourceServer methods that called Init. Any transient indexing/watcher failure at process start now prevents the server from being constructed at all; previously a failed Init was retried on the next request, so a slow or flaky index backend during a rolling deploy takes the storage server down instead of degrading per-request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from per-method calls to `NewResourceServer`: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and the per-request `if err := s.Init(ctx)` blocks were removed from many RPC handlers. This does change the failure boundary: an init failure now prevents constructing/starting the server, whereas previously the server could be created and the first call into a method would fail. However, the finding’s claim that a failed init was “retried on the next request” is not supported by the diff: `Init` uses `s.initOnce.Do(...)`, so initialization would not be retried per request; it would just keep returning the stored `s.initErr`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test change in this diff is a t.Skip() that disables the integration test for postgres with a TODO, removing CI coverage for a DB backend while the diff restructures server lifecycle (Init moved from lazy per-request calls into NewResourceServer, watcher/search init reordered). Any regression from the init reordering (e.g. Init failing at construction time, or the watcher now initialized after search) will no longer be caught by this integration test for postgres in CI; the skip masks an environment-specific failure ('Works locally') instead of fixing it, so the suite silently loses coverage while passing green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new postgres-specific `t.Skip()` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`, explicitly disabling that integration test for postgres in CI (“test not working with postgres in Drone”). At the same time, the diff makes a nontrivial lifecycle change: `s.Init(ctx)` is now called in `NewResourceServer` and removed from per-request methods, and `Init` reorders initialization (search init before watcher). Skipping the only changed integration test for postgres does reduce CI coverage for this backend while these init-order changes land, potentially letting regressions slip through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init is now called unconditionally in NewResourceServer, converting a previously lazy, per-request-retried initialization failure into a hard startup failure. If search.init or initWatcher fails at process start (transient DB/search-store unavailability, partially built index dir), the resource server cannot be constructed at all, so the pod crash-loops instead of serving degraded traffic and retrying; during a rolling deploy this turns a recoverable condition into an outage window.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows NewResourceServer now calling `s.Init(ctx)` and returning `nil, err` on failure (`pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`), while all per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This is a concrete behavioral change from lazy init-on-first-use to eager init-at-construction, meaning init failures (e.g., `s.search.init(ctx)` or `s.initWatcher()`) will prevent server construction rather than allowing the process to start and defer failure until first use. Whether that is desirable is an availability/architecture concern, not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the function-wide cacheMu lock in BuildIndex makes the b.cache[key] read and the build itself run concurrently for the same key, so two concurrent callers both construct an index for the same file-backed path and the second bleve.New(dir) fails with 'index already exists', and the unsynchronized map read/write on b.cache is a data race that can panic with 'concurrent map read and map write'. Two concurrent searches (or a search racing a WriteEvent-driven rebuild) for the same namespace/resource either crash the process on the map race or return a spurious build error to callers who previously serialized behind the lock; the cache dedup that justified the lock is now gone, so every concurrent caller pays the full reindex cost.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function, serializing concurrent builds for the same key. The diff removes that function-wide lock and only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end. That means two concurrent callers can both proceed to `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for the same `dir` (derived solely from `key`), so they can race creating the same on-disk index path; the second creator can fail because the index directory has been created by the first. Even though the final cache write is now mutex-protected, the build/creation work is no longer deduped/serialized, so concurrent callers can trigger spurious build failures and redundant full rebuild costs that were previously avoided by the lock.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Moving Init (which includes the full search index build and watcher startup) from the per-request lazy path into NewResourceServer turns a transient backend failure at construction time into a hard startup failure with no retry, whereas the removed per-request Init calls would have retried on the next request. A momentary database unavailability during process start now prevents the resource server from being constructed at all (process fails to start), instead of the previous behavior where the first request would re-attempt lazy initialization; conversely, any caller that constructs the server before the backing store is reachable can never recover because the retry points (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/IsHealthy) were all deleted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization earlier: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails, and the per-RPC `Init` calls in `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob` were removed. This does change behavior so an init failure (e.g., during search index init or watcher startup) can prevent server construction / process startup. However, the finding’s claim about “retry on the next request” is not supported: `Init` is guarded by `s.initOnce.Do(...)` (visible in the diff hunk around `Init`), so even previously, once `Init` ran and failed, later requests would not re-run initialization. The main actionable issue is the potentially intentional fail-fast startup behavior change, not loss of retry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Init sets s.initErr and only logs it; when called from NewResourceServer the returned error path depends entirely on initErr propagating, but if any earlier step set initErr the search init and initWatcher are silently skipped with no per-step log, and IsHealthy (init check removed at line ~940) now reports diagnostics.IsHealthy without any indication that the search index or watcher never initialized. A server whose watcher failed to start (initErr set) serves reads/writes from the SQL backend while the search index permanently diverges from the data, and health checks report healthy, so operators get search results that silently miss recent writes with no signal that init ever failed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes NewResourceServer to call `s.Init(ctx)` and return an error if it fails (server.go @@255+), and removes per-RPC `Init` calls. Given this, a server with `initErr` set (e.g., watcher/search init failure) should not be successfully constructed via NewResourceServer, so it would not continue serving reads/writes while search diverges, nor would health checks run on an uninitialized instance created this way. The claim that init failures are only logged and then the server continues operating/health-checking as healthy is not supported by the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Reordering initWatcher to run after s.search.init lengthens the window during which writes are not being watched while the (potentially long) full index build reads its snapshot, so events committed between the build's data read and the watcher's start position can be silently dropped from the index. The larger the tenant (longer init), the more writes fall into the unwatched gap; combined with the acknowledged 'TODO, check last RV' gap in bleve.go, those resources are missing from search results until a full rebuild, with no error or metric indicating the miss.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly reorders initialization in `(*server).Init`: it now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (see `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`). Since `s.search.init(ctx)` can involve a potentially long index build (and `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` constructs indexes and only later updates the cache), starting the watcher later plausibly increases a window where external writes/updates could occur before the watcher is running. However, the claim that events are "silently dropped" between a snapshot read and the watch start position is not directly verifiable from the shown diff because `initWatcher()` implementation and how it chooses its start cursor/RV are not included.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log computes duration via time.Now().Unix() subtraction, so any init under one second logs duration_secs=0 and the IndexCreationTime histogram records 0, making the new observability signal useless for all but the slowest builds. Operators tuning index-build performance get a metric quantized to whole seconds (typically 0), and cannot distinguish a fast init from a failed/no-op one using this log line.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, init() uses start := time.Now().Unix() and end := time.Now().Unix(), then logs duration_secs as end-start and observes IndexCreationTime with float64(end-start). This is whole-second granularity, so any init completing in <1s will log/record 0, reducing the usefulness of the new log line and the metric for performance tuning. It’s an observability-quality issue rather than a functional defect, and the quantization for the metric already existed, but the new log line repeats/exposes it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Changing to ctx, span := b.tracer.Start in GetResourceStats rewires the rest of the function's queries into the span's context, so the SQL stats query now runs under a child span context that will carry the span's cancellation into the request — harmless if the caller's ctx is the request ctx, but it means an early span.End() ordering mistake or span-based timeout would now cancel the DB query, a semantic change with no test coverage in this diff. If any future refactor moves span.End() earlier or attaches a span-scoped deadline, the stats query starts failing with context cancellation in ways the previous shadowed-ctx version did not; no regression test in this diff guards GetResourceStats behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go`, the change from `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)` to `ctx, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)` only propagates the returned context (which typically just embeds the span for trace propagation) to subsequent calls. Nothing in the diff shows that `tracer.Start` introduces a new cancellation/timeout, nor does `span.End()` cancel a context. The finding’s core claim that this rewiring makes DB queries fail via “span’s cancellation” or `span.End()` ordering is not supported by the diff and misrepresents how span contexts normally behave.
